description: AquaCosmos is a 3D rainwater simulator for Cyprus using NASA GPM and SRTM data. It visualizes how rainfall flows downhill across the island and tracks how much water is retained versus lost to the sea.
summary: AquaCosmos is a free, browser-based “data detective” that lets students and the public investigate whether Cyprus’s climate is changing, using real NASA data. Users choose a question, a place (whole island, Troodos, Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca or Paphos) and a time range. The tool analyses NASA GPM IMERG, MERRA-2 and FLDAS monthly records in the browser and returns a plain-language verdict: the rate of change per decade (Sen’s slope), and whether it is statistically significant (Mann-Kendall, p < 0.05) or still hidden in natural year-to-year noise. A 3D terrain map, a case file and a 17-step guided tour make the investigation easy to follow.For the challenge “Be an Earth System Trend Detective!”, our analysis found that Cyprus has warmed about +1.5 °C since 1980 (p < 0.001), while yearly rainfall shows no significant change (p = 0.77) and dry-season rainfall is falling, significantly in Limassol and Paphos.It matters because it teaches the difference between a real trend and noise, and shows uncertainty honestly: all 23 results are displayed, and only 4 pass p < 0.05.
details: AquaCosmos is a free, browser-based “data detective” tool for students and the public. A visitor picks a question (for example, “Is dry-season rainfall decreasing?”), a place (whole island, Troodos, Nicosia, Limassol, Larnaca or Paphos) and a time range. The tool analyses NASA monthly records directly in the browser. It answers in plain language: how fast the variable is changing per decade, how large the change is over the whole record, and whether the change is statistically real or still hidden in natural year-to-year noise.
